surprises.title: Wall turns out load-bearing
surprises.description: Uh oh. The joists above sit right on top of this wall. It's holding up the second floor.

options.text: Knock it out and add a few 2x4s later
Rebuild the entire second-floor framing
Hire an engineer to design a beam

surprises.title: Footing is too weak
surprises.description: The new post lands on a slab that's barely 4 inches thick. That's not a footing, that's a sidewalk.

options.text: Set the post on a stack of pavers
Replace the whole foundation
Pour a new footing under the post

surprises.title: Wires appear in wall
surprises.description: Surprise! Three circuits run through this wall, including the one for the fridge.

options.text: Have an electrician reroute the circuits
Tape the wire ends and leave them hanging
Rewire the whole house

surprises.title: Electrical panel is full
surprises.description: The electrician frowns at your panel. It's full, and it might be older than you.

options.text: Double up wires on one breaker
Go solar with battery backup
Upgrade the electrical panel

surprises.title: Vent stack blocks removal
surprises.description: Bad news. A big vent pipe runs right up the middle of the wall.

options.text: Box it into a decorative column
Redo all the upstairs bathroom plumbing
Reroute the vent to a nearby wall

surprises.title: Asbestos shows up
surprises.description: The test kit is back. The old joint compound has asbestos. Fun!

options.text: Hire a licensed abatement crew
Sell the house
Wear a dust mask and keep swinging

surprises.title: Floors don't match
surprises.description: With the wall gone, oak meets laminate in a very straight, very obvious line.

options.text: Cover the seam with a big rug
Replace the floors in both rooms
Install a transition strip

surprises.title: Ceiling texture clashes
surprises.description: Your ceiling patch is smooth. The rest of the ceiling is popcorn. Everyone will notice.

options.text: Spray matching texture on the patch
Scrape and retexture the whole ceiling
Leave it, nobody looks up

surprises.title: Island fever strikes
surprises.description: Standing in the new open space, you suddenly need a kitchen island. Need.

options.text: Build an island with a sink this month
Sketch it for next year
Push the dining table over and call it an island

surprises.title: Partner hears a squeak
surprises.description: Your partner: "Since the tools are out, the bedroom door is squeaking again."

options.text: Replace every door in the house
Take the door off and leave it in the garage
Lube the hinge after cleanup

surprises.title: Beam won't fit flush
surprises.description: The engineer's beam is deeper than your ceiling joists. It's not going to hide up there.

options.text: Use a dropped beam below the ceiling
Notch the beam so it fits
Raise the second floor

surprises.title: Duct runs through wall
surprises.description: There's an HVAC duct inside the wall feeding the upstairs bedroom. It was not on the plans.

options.text: Replace the whole HVAC system
Reroute the duct through the ceiling
Cut the duct and cap both ends

surprises.title: Vent route hits a joist
surprises.description: The new vent path runs straight into a floor joist. Naturally.

options.text: Cut through the joist
Route around the joist with fittings
Move the upstairs bathroom

surprises.title: Abatement crew is booked
surprises.description: The abatement crew can't come for three weeks, and the wall is half open.

options.text: Clean it up yourself with a shop vac
Seal off the area with plastic and wait
Pay triple for a rush crew

surprises.title: Floor gap appears
surprises.description: Where the wall stood, a 5-inch strip of bare subfloor stares back at you.

options.text: Fill it with wood filler
Replace the floors in both rooms
Weave in boards salvaged from a closet

surprises.title: Flooring is discontinued
surprises.description: You finally find your exact flooring online. Discontinued in 2014.

options.text: Patch with a close-enough board
Refloor the entire house
Hunt for leftover boxes on resale sites

surprises.title: Ceiling gap appears
surprises.description: The top plate is gone, leaving a long, ragged slot across the ceiling.

options.text: Cover it with a strip of trim
Add blocking and patch with drywall
Leave it open as a design feature

surprises.title: Popcorn ceiling tests positive
surprises.description: You sent a popcorn sample to the lab just in case. It came back with asbestos.

options.text: Have it abated before any scraping
Drywall over every ceiling in the house
Scrape it wet and hope for the best

surprises.title: Recessed light itch
surprises.description: The ceiling is already patched. What if... can lights. Everywhere.

options.text: Run extension cords across the ceiling
Plan them for a future project
Cut in twelve can lights tonight

surprises.title: Hallway looks tired
surprises.description: The fresh open room makes the hallway look gray and gloomy.

options.text: Hang more art to distract from it
Touch up the worst scuffs
Repaint the whole house

video.title: Removing a wall? Watch this first

ask.question: How do I remove the wall between my kitchen and living room?
ask.answer: Great project! 1. Cut the drywall. 2. Take out the studs. 3. Patch and paint. You've got this!
ask.skipped: It skipped checking if the wall is load-bearing, and the header beam.
